analysis: This batch contains only documentation. changelog.d/ssd-read-single-copy.md (head 1-8) is a new note. It says SSD cache reads now keep each encrypted chunk in the buffer it was read into, without a second copy, when one read returns the whole chunk. docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md changes the date (line 3) and the Streaming read row (line 65), which now cites SSDBlockStore.readExactly. Neither document changes the DBK3 format, AAD, HMAC lookup naming, KEK handling, TTL or staging bounds, so T-041 mitigations (a)-(e) are unaffected as documented. The change applies to ciphertext buffers before AES-GCM authentication. The docs claim no plaintext exposure and no change to authentication order. The actual Swift implementation (SSDBlockStore.readExactly, SSDBlockChunkCursor, SSDBlockStore+Streaming.readStreaming) is not in this batch, so these behaviours are unverified, not proven safe. Integration should check that readExactly: (1) still enforces the exact requested length; (2) handles a partial read with a bounded loop; (3) keeps the retry raw-byte charge before allocation (ssd-kv-cache.md base line 278: SSDCheckpointReadBudget.beforeRead, plus the one-byte EOF allowance); (4) checks the chunk length cap (maximumChunkBytes 16 MiB) before reading; (5) does not return an over-long or under-length buffer, or an aliased slice that later reads mutate before GCM opens it. No regression is identified from the docs alone.
